The Department of Defense (DoD) developed the Military and Family Life Counseling (MFLC) program as an initiative of the Office of the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Military Community and Family Policy (MC&FP), facilitating private and confidential Non-Medical Counseling services.

The MFLC Program was established to expand access to confidential, face-to-face counseling and reduce the barriers and stigma often associated with seeking counseling support.
Currently, the MFLC Program provides non-medical counseling, consultation, and outreach services to more than 200 military installations or nearby civilian communities located in most all the 50 states, the District of Columbia, United States (U.S.) territories and commonwealths, and over 25 foreign countries including areas considered hazardous duty/danger zones.

Title:
Contract Program Manager

In this position, your work will have a profound impact on the country’s most critical role – protecting our national security.

Why Join Us?
- Innovative Projects: KBR’s work is at the forefront of engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity solutions.
- Collaborative Environment: Be part of a dynamic team that thrives on collaboration and innovation, fostering a supportive and intellectually stimulating workplace.
- Impactful Work: Your contributions will be pivotal in designing and optimizing defense systems that ensure national security and shape the future of space defense.

This is a contingent position based upon contract award

KBR is seeking an Expert-Level Contract Program Manager (CPM) to support a procurement providing Systems Engineering and Integration (SE&I) support to an IC/DOD government customer within the Washington DC Metropolitan area.
The CPM will be the interface with the government customer regarding contract activities and programmatic, and overall contract or program performance. To achieve this, the CPM shall maintain regular communication with the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) and Government Program Manager (PM), keeping them informed of relevant contractor related information especially significant risks and issues and the associated resolution plans and status.
The CPM will be responsible for day-to-day contract activities to include formulating and enforcing work deliverables, assigning schedules, reviewing work discrepancies, supervising contractor personnel and communicating policies objectives and goals of the organization to the contractor team. The CPM will also help establish both technical and business goals in consultation with top management and make detailed plans for the accomplishment of the established goals.

Primary Responsibilities:
- Ensuring the timely execution of all financial, staffing and administrative contract actions.
- Lead the team assisting the customer in the development, implementation, and adoption of the Digital Engineering (DE) environment, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) practices, and Digital Twin capabilities
- Serve as the primary point of contact with the government customer and key figures and offices (including the Chief Engineer and Program Executive Offices (PEOs)) within the organization.
- Provide contract management support to the Program(s) PMO to ensure the timely execution of all financial, staffing and administrative contract actions.
- Provide program management support to include cost, schedule, risk and performance management of all staff and work activities.
- Ensure contractor personnel are qualified to perform the assigned task and that potential personnel problems are pre-empted.
- Ensure contract tasks are completed within the specified timelines.
- Establish and implement processes and procedures enabling the rapid response to surge requirements for increased contract personnel.
- Ensure programmatic alignment and adherence to the customer’s visions and priorities.
- Ensure the accuracy, quality, configuration management and timely delivery of all required deliverables to include the Monthly Financial Report, Monthly Staffing Report, Monthly Activity Report, Quarterly Program Management Review materials, and as required Trip Reports, Briefings, Evaluations, Technical Assignments, White Papers or other Government requested deliverables necessary for the successful execution and/or completion of work activities.
- Plan and execute Quarterly Program Reviews to provide the Government customer(s) an comprehensive understanding of the health/status of all activities.
- Coordination program management activities between various offices within the customer organization.
-  Perform day-to-day contractual and programmatic management of the TO.
- Monitor performance metrics, SLAs, and KPIs and report progress to government customer leadership

Required Qualifications:
- Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, or related STEM degree program, or equivalent Expert level experience as a Program Manager.
- Expert-level experience (10 years or more) as a Program Manager in terms of managing program level cost, schedule, performance, and risk management for a development, engineering, or other Information Technology DoD or IC program.
- Project Management Professional (PMP), DAWIA Level III certification in Program Management, or similar professional certification in program management or demonstrated experience applying Project Management tools and techniques.
- Extensive experience working with Customer, and other IC\DoD mission partners.
- Ability to engage with senior government stakeholders and lead cross-functional teams.
- Expert experience as a Program Manager in terms of cost, schedule, performance, and risk management.
- Demonstrated experience in engineering, Enterprise engineering, design and analysis of IT or related systems experience in all phases of design, development, analysis and documentation, and development of standards and guidelines for tasks being performed.
- Expert-level working experience in government or industry in DoD/IC Acquisition Process or PPBES.
- Active TS/SCI required
- Experience with Digital Engineering (DE) and Model Based System Engineering (MBSE)

Desired Skills and Experience:
- Knowledge of the geospatial intelligence mission and its contributions to the Intelligence Community.
- Knowledge of the National System for Geospatial Intelligence.
- Working knowledge of Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), processes, tools and languages.
- Experience with the development and/or review of cost estimates and the associated technical work scope necessary to achieve stated objectives.
- Experience in tailoring and using both Agile and Waterfall development methodologies
- Experience with the identification of technical issues and proactive communication of possible impacts.
- Experience in performing validation and verification of various engineering results and deliverables to ensure the highest quality results against customer requirements.
- Experience advising and assisting the government leadership team in achieving their mission objectives by leveraging the combine resources within the government team and their industrial base
- Basic understanding of cloud technologies, DevSecOps, CI/CD pipelines, and AI/ML integration.

$177,300 - $216,600
This range is for the Virginia area only

Title:
Program Manager

Who We Are
KBR Government Solutions delivers full life cycle professional and technical solutions that improve operational readiness and drive innovation. Our solutions help ensure mission success on land, air, sea, space and cyberspace for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA and other federal agencies. KBR’s areas of expertise include engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT and cybersecurity.  KBR strives to create a safer, more secure and sustainable world by bringing together the best and brightest to deliver technologies and solutions that help our customers accomplish their most critical missions and objectives.

The Mission Ahead
This role is with KBR’s Government Solutions U.S. division.  At KBR Government Solutions, we don't just envision a world that's safer, more secure, and sustainable - we create it. Our legacy of delivering advanced full life cycle professional and technical solutions is matched only by our commitment to operational readiness and innovation. As stewards of critical missions for the Department of Defense, Intelligence Community, NASA, and other key federal entities, we excel in engineering, logistics, operations, science, program management, mission IT, and cybersecurity. United in our quest for excellence, KBR stands at the vanguard, ready to transform possibilities into impactful realities for a better tomorrow.

Who You Are
A forward-looking leader, you stay abreast of industry and academic trends in program management, applying advanced tools and practices to your work. You possess a solid foundation in business concepts and accounting principles necessary for meticulous project cost and budgetary oversight. Your role often involves strategic interface with business unit Controllers and Marketing teams, leveraging opportunities and managing business pursuits with informed judgement. An in-depth understanding of all facets of facilities management, and business operations is fundamental to your role, as is extensive experience in program management and progressive leadership responsibility. Your qualifications may also be matched by substantial professional experience in lieu of formal education.

Operations run 24x7 therefore your responsibilities extend beyond traditional boundaries to ensure continuous availability of critical systems and the facilities’ infrastructure while maintaining exceptional appearance and first-class maintenance of facilities to provide outstanding customer service to high-level dignitaries and senior executive stakeholders.

An adept leader, you're no stranger to navigating large-scale projects with finesse. Your expertise in resource management, strategic planning, and process improvement is surpassed only by your commitment to balancing stakeholder expectations with concrete business outcomes. Your eye for compliance and your strategic mindset ensures that each contractual requirement is not just met but exceeded. As a navigator of complexity, you are prepared to architect the integration of project data, optimize resource allocation, and achieve operational excellence across the board.

This role will be located in Alice Springs, Australia at a 4,400-acre facility with approximately 687,000 square feet of mission and support space.  The Program Manager will be expected to travel between our facilities in Alice Springs and the local area.   This position is expected to be onsite 100% and is contingent upon contract award.

What You’ll Do
As a Program Manager (PM), you will:
- Experience working in 24x7 mission-critical environments supporting facilities construction, operations, and maintenance, and support services where continuous availability of facility infrastructure is essential and of the highest priority

- Display strong technical, programmatic and personal leadership skills

- Knowledgeable of the guidelines provided by the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR)

- Professional certification such as PMP, CFM, PE, FAC-P/PM Mid-Level, or Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Level 2 certification in Program Management

- Responsible for the execution of the SOW within the cost and on schedule to include but not limited to: Ensuring community of support during Contractor personnel change; Interfacing Contractor Officer (CO), COTR, and Chief of Facilities; Delivery of all contract requirements; Managing subcontracts and be responsible for the performance and conduct of subcontractor personnel

- Strategic Oversight: Command the planning, resourcing, and execution across multiple programs/projects, ensuring alignment with business and product line strategies

- Financial Stewardship: Scrutinize and sanction financial frameworks and reports, maintaining the integrity of management reserves and expenditure

- Holistic Integration: Champion cross-functional team efforts to deliver a synchronized service that addresses every angle of the Government's requirements

- Risk Management: Strategize and allocate funds for risk mitigation, safeguarding project outcomes

- Communication: Communicate effectively with all customers, and maintain a transparent and proactive dialogue with the Government, ensuring clarity and prompt resolution of issues

- Customer Service: Demonstrate strong customer service skills

- Regulatory Adherence: Vigilantly enforce all contractual, regulatory, and compliance mandates in partnership with the contracts team

- Possess an active TS/SCI U.S. Security Clearance with Counterintelligence polygraph or host nation PV clearance

- A minimum of 10 years of prior relevant PM and Intelligence Community (IC) experience managing a large (250+ person) multi-disciplinary workforce including tradesmen, engineers, warehousing personnel, and other base operating support staff

Preferred Qualifications
- 10 years of experience in formal management, leading a team

- 5 years of experience working with business strategy

- 5 years of experience developing project execution plans, schedules, and budgets

- 5 years of experience supporting the Federal and/or Intelligence Community

- 5 years of experience with long range business plans

- Experience building and sustaining high performing integrated teams

- Knowledge of process improvement models (e.g. LEAN/Six Sigma, ISO 9000)

- Proficient knowledge and experience in the use of project management concepts to manage items including, but not limited to: project schedule, scope, cost, risk, and deliverables and related metrics

- Experience planning and implementing large-scale facility and logistics projects

- Knowledge of U.S. government exercise or crisis management communities and experience planning, coordinating and executing support to special events

- Familiarity with 24/7/365 operational environment

The ideal candidate is a former senior AOC, air operations, or operational C2 leader who understands how an AOC actually functions under real mission tempo. This person must understand how government programs are run from the government side: cost, schedule, performance, risk, requirements, stakeholder alignment, contractor accountability, operational readiness, and the realities of fielded weapon system sustainment.  The candidate will exhibit collaborative leadership with the government program office, operators, teammates, and the requirements community.

1. Mission-Facing Program Leadership
·          Lead KBR's Falconer/AOC program strategy and execution activities, ensuring alignment between customer objectives, operational needs, and program performance.

·          Evaluate proposed technical and programmatic approaches to ensure they are operationally practical and support mission execution.
·          Build and maintain trusted relationships with government stakeholders, operational users, teammates, and internal leadership.

·          Apply extensive program management experience to drive successful execution of cost, schedule, performance, and risk objectives.

Title:
APS-3: Deputy Program Manager

Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR!

Program Summary
The Readiness and Sustainment (R&S) business unit is dedicated to ensuring operational excellence and compliance in occupational safety, health, and environmental. Our goal is to maintain a robust safety culture that adheres to all regulatory standards. We strive to create a safe and healthy work environment for all employees, both domestically and internationally.

Job Summary
This position supports the Army Prepositioned Stocks – Afloat (APS-3) Program and the Presidential Drawdown (PD) mission located in Goose Creek, SC on Naval Weapons Station Charleston/Joint Base Charleston. The Program Manager (PM) serves as the Site Manager at AFSBn-CHS and single overall manager and the point of contact for all contractor operations and management functions. As the deputy to the program manager, the ideal candidate will have extensive experience managing Army maintenance and/or supply operations in uniform or as a contractor – technical schooling or experience with US Army Logistics Standard Army Management Information Systems (STAMIS) is a plus.  The Deputy Program Manager must have strong oral/written communication skills and must have experience managing a large workforce under a Cost-Plus contract or similar environment.

Roles and Responsibilities
- The Deputy Program Manager will be primarily responsible for the Operations, Maintenance, and Logistics Departments with overall planning and coordination of APS-3 ship “maintenance cycles” – download support; port support activities; reception; accountability; maintenance; reconstitution; staging; convoy to wharf; port support activity; and upload support.

- Manage all logistics, maintenance, and readiness for APS-3 unit sets and other assigned equipment in GCSS-A

- Manages the process of compiling, analyzing and interpreting statistical data related to contract operations and initiates and manages corrective actions.

- Assist in the planning coordination and successful completion of actions related to the Performance Work Statement (PWS).

- Develops and maintains a strong effective relationship with the customer acting as primary interface for current and future operations planning and execution.

- Participates in planning processes with customer providing input on matters related to the responsibility inherent in the contract.

- Ensures submission of required reports and CDRL reports to the customer and receives required reports from site managers and program management staff.

- Ensures compliance with ISO 9001:2015 standards as they pertain to the entire program.

- Promotes a Zero Harm safety culture.

- Performs other related duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications
- Must be a U.S. Citizen.

- Must be able to obtain and maintain a Common Access Card (CAC)

- Must obtain and maintain local base access.

- Must possess a valid State Driver’s License.

- Must have a minimum of Bachelor’s Degree in Logistics Management, Production Management, Operations Management, or Business Management or engineering field (e.g. Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or Electrical Engineering). Applicable specialized military or military contracting experience can be used in lieu of formal post high school education on a one-to-one basis.

- Must have a minimum of 10 Years of experience in a related field with 7 years in a management or supervisory capacity.

- Secret Clearance Required (Current or Prior).

- Must be able to meet the physical/medical deployment requirements for US Army Contractors.

Preferred Qualifications
- Excellent leadership and team building skills

- Strong analytical skills for data compilation and trend analysis.

- Excellent coordination and communication skills.

The Operations Manager works closely with engineering, cybersecurity, and program management teams to ensure operational excellence, compliance, and customer satisfaction.
